# Adapt Rust bridge targets and package the resulting OH library

## Platform difference

Reusing a Rust core still requires a matching OH toolchain target, Dart/Rust bridge generation and native library packaging.

## Implementation

PixEz adds the OH Cargokit target and aligns its Rust flutter_rust_bridge version/generated files. Draftmark, InkNote and Nexora supply local Rust builder modules and keep business/storage/compiler logic in Rust behind Flutter. NipaPlay invokes Cargo from the native build and copies its artifact into Hvigor output because its selected integration lacks an OH runner. LocalSend vendors FRB loader handling while the HTTP core remains a submodule.

## Applicability

These are several version-specific build strategies, not interchangeable snippets. Match target triple, ABI, generator/runtime versions, dependent libraries and the actual Flutter OH embedding.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Uninitialized submodules, developer-local bridge paths and bundled binaries are reproducibility boundaries. Native source reuse does not prove the library loads on a device or that all features of the Rust core work on OH.

## Verification

Build from explicit inputs, inspect packaged libraries and exported symbols, initialize the bridge in a release HAP and call representative functions including error and large-data cases.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
